body: Dragon Quest Monsters: Joker is Tose's Nintendo DS role-playing game following a young scout who recruits familiar Dragon Quest creatures to fight on his behalf. Travelling between the islands of Green Bays supplies the encounters needed to build a team for the monster-scouting competition. The subseries moves into three-dimensional surroundings, with monsters visible in the landscape before battle begins. Its central pleasure is developing the creatures normally met as opponents, turning a new encounter into the possibility of another companion and another way to arrange the next fight.

A battle party contains up to three monsters, which can receive direct commands or follow selected tactics. The human scout supports the group with items rather than joining the attacks. Monsters encountered in the landscape can be avoided or approached, and attacking from behind can provide an early advantage. The visible encounters give exploration a practical choice before the turn-based system takes over. A player can seek a particular creature, prepare for the meeting or continue toward another destination instead of accepting every battle as an unseen interruption.

Jet-ski routes connect the main islands, with occasional uncharted destinations adding another reason to pay attention during travel. Building a useful collection gives those excursions a purpose beyond simply following the tournament route. The original online system also allowed a team to be ranked and matched against downloaded opponents, extending the test beyond the main adventure. Joker connects exploration with preparation through these different encounters: what is found while travelling becomes part of a team whose strengths can then be tested in another setting against a different arrangement of monsters.
